raw: 38.1 Understanding Neurocognitive Mechanisms of Cognitive Security (Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews, 2025)[^176][^177]
teaching_note: The review proposes a framework spanning executive, affective, and integrative mechanisms and explicitly says the drivers and neurophysiology are incompletely understood. A mechanism hypothesis explains a possible process; a candidate measure is an observation proposed for study; a validated biomarker requires evidence for a specified use. Publisher and PubMed records refer to the same review, not independent replications, and the framework does not validate person-level vulnerability, credibility, or diagnostic judgments [@ageint176; @ageint177].
title: Understanding Neurocognitive Mechanisms of Cognitive Security (Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews, 2025)

raw: 38.1.1 Executive Brain Systems and Vulnerability to Information Threats[^177]
teaching_note: Executive functions include maintaining task goals, holding and updating information, and inhibiting an irrelevant response; this is cognitive research vocabulary, not a software vulnerability record. An error on a demanding task may reflect unclear instructions, competing demands, or unfamiliarity rather than deficient executive capacity. Neither a task mistake nor a neural signal licenses a conclusion about an individual's susceptibility or fitness [@ageint177].
title: Executive Brain Systems: Research on Information-Related Tasks

raw: 38.1.2 Affective Systems: Emotional Exploitation in Manipulation[^177]
teaching_note: Affective processing concerns emotional salience and valuation, which can matter in both legitimate communication and misleading messages. A truthful warning may be emotional; a calm presentation may be false. The discriminating question is whether evidence supports the content and the hypothesized mechanism, not whether a reader's reaction proves manipulation or reveals private intent [@ageint177].
title: Affective Systems: Emotion and Information Processing

raw: 38.1.3 Integrative Systems: Brain Network Interactions During Threat Exposure[^177]
teaching_note: Integrative accounts examine interactions among cognitive processes rather than assigning a complex judgment to a single brain location. Inferring a specific mental state from activation associated with many tasks is reverse inference; transferring a group association to an individual is a further unsupported step. The review's proposed framework motivates research questions, not a surveillance system or a proven causal chain from exposure through brain activity to belief [@ageint177].
title: Integrative Systems: Proposed Brain-Network Interactions

teaching_note: **Completed synthetic abstract critique.** A supplied fictional abstract reports that 20 simulated task records show higher EEG feature X during misleading than neutral notices; no held-out validation, individual ground truth, or intervention is supplied. The completed review records an observed task association, a candidate attention mechanism, and alternatives of task difficulty and stimulus differences; it rejects the proposed conclusion that X diagnoses susceptibility. A new card says the misleading notices were twice as long, so the interpretation narrows further to an unresolved length/difficulty confound. Decision: hold the biomarker and intervention claims pending matched-task and independent-validation evidence; no real EEG is collected and no individual is classified [@ageint177].
title: Candidate Neuromarkers: Validation and Inference Limits

raw: 38.2 Neuro-Cognitive Approaches to Cybersecurity: Systematic Review (Emerald, 2025)[^178]
teaching_note: The raw heading retains an inherited 2025 attribution; the local source description identifies a January-2026 article, and the direct journal record was unavailable for resolving online-first versus issue dates. A systematic review can catalogue proposed measures and applications without validating each one. Separate controlled-task research, interface design hypotheses, and proposed insider-risk uses; the last does not justify personnel screening, inferred deception, or physiological monitoring in this curriculum [@ageint178].
title: Neuro-Cognitive Approaches to Cybersecurity: Systematic Review

raw: 38.3 Cognitive Load in Intelligence Community Settings (NCSU Survey, 2024)[^179]
teaching_note: Cognitive load concerns demands on limited processing resources; subjective workload is a person's reported experience of a task, not a direct readout of brain capacity. Select a measure by task, intended construct, validity evidence, feasibility, and pilot fit rather than popularity or apparent objectivity. The survey's coverage of literature through 2024 is not itself its publication date or proof that a measure transfers to every analytic task [@ageint179].
title: Cognitive Load in Intelligence Community Settings: Measurement Survey

teaching_note: A catalogue count describes measurement diversity, not 129 validated interchangeable instruments. Questionnaires report perceived demand; task measures report outcomes such as errors and latency; physiological measures record signals affected by many processes. Agreement among measures can be informative, but disagreement should prompt a construct/task review rather than averaging them into an invented susceptibility score [@ageint179].
title: Catalogued Metrics: Questionnaire, Biometric, Task-Performance

raw: 38.3.2 NASA-TLX and Its Intelligence Analytic Applications[^179]
teaching_note: NASA's [instrument description](https://www.nasa.gov/human-systems-integration-division/nasa-task-load-index-tlx/) identifies mental, physical, and temporal demand, performance, effort, and frustration; its weighted procedure is not the same as an unweighted raw mean. For a supplied fictional 20-minute document-comparison task, post-task ratings are respectively 60, 10, 70, 30, 60, 40 on declared 0–100 scales (low to high demand/effort/frustration, good to poor performance): raw mean = 270/6 = 45. All dimensions are present; if one were missing, report an incomplete record rather than silently imputing or comparing unlike totals. This is a scoring illustration, not administration guidance or an overload threshold; performance self-rating must remain separate from independently checked errors [@ageint179].
title: NASA-TLX: Subjective Workload and Declared Scoring

raw: 38.3.3 Eye Tracking and Heart Rate Variability for Analyst Overload Detection[^179]
teaching_note: Eye movements and heart-rate variability are candidate task-sensitive signals, not specific tests for overload, truthfulness, intent, illness, or readiness for work. Lighting, movement, interface layout, physical activity, and measurement quality can complicate interpretation; a baseline does not eliminate all confounding. Prefer supplied synthetic task/error logs and voluntary workload reports here, with no student biometric collection or person-level surveillance; missing task-fit validation means the physiological inference remains unestablished [@ageint179].
title: Eye Tracking and Heart-Rate Variability: Workload Research Limits

raw: 38.4 Information Overload and Cognitive Bias in Intelligence Analysis[^180]
teaching_note: Information volume and biased reasoning are distinct: more documents can add redundancy rather than independent evidence, while a short packet can still anchor a judgment. In the fictional document task, five copied notices should become one dependency group before a reviewer asks what contrary evidence is missing. The SpecialEurasia account summarizes Heuer; it is not a primary neuroscience experiment or evidence that reducing every workload score improves analytic quality [@ageint180].
title: Information Overload and Cognitive Bias in Intelligence Analysis

raw: 38.5 Decision-Making Under Uncertainty: Neural Mechanisms and Intelligence Implications
teaching_note: An uncertain decision can be analyzed at behavioral, computational, and neural levels, but a model at one level does not automatically validate another. A defensible analytic output states alternatives, missing information, and a reversible hold decision without inferring a reader's internal state. The inherited foreign-influence policy citations supply policy context, not direct neural-mechanism evidence; retain that gap rather than inventing a brain-based explanation [@ageint177].
title: Decision-Making Under Uncertainty: Neural Hypotheses and Analytic Limits
